name: Ebed
overview: Ebed is a male biblical figure identified primarily as the father of Gaal. Beyond this familial connection, Scripture provides no additional details regarding his tribe or other personal notes. His mention is concise, emphasizing his paternal role within the narrative.
namesAndTitles: The name Ebed is a proper name meaning 'servant.' This meaning is given without indication that the name was divinely assigned. It simply reflects a common Hebrew name, highlighting a humble or service-oriented identity.
familyAndRelationships: Ebed is recorded in Scripture as the father of Gaal, establishing a direct paternal relationship. No other family relationships are documented for him beyond this connection.
scriptureSignificance: Ebed's significance in the biblical narrative is linked to his role as the father of Gaal, who appears in the context of Judges 9:26. Although Ebed himself is not a prominent actor, his mention grounds Gaal’s identity and lineage within the story, contributing to the genealogical and relational framework of the events described.
